summary.headline: Dalmia Bharat Q1 FY27 volumes rose 9% YoY while EBITDA fell 11% QoQ to INR805 crores; Jaypee acquisition closed at INR2,850 crore EV.
summary.overview: Volumes grew 9% YoY despite state elections in key markets, and premium products reached 25% of mix. Revenue rose 7% YoY to INR3,890 crores and realisations improved 6% QoQ on price hikes of INR10-15/t in South and INR15-20/t in East. EBITDA per ton rose 3% QoQ to INR1,055, but absolute EBITDA fell 11% QoQ to INR805 crores on lower volumes and fuel/packing cost inflation. The Jaypee Cement acquisition (5.2 Mt cement, 3.3 Mt clinker, Central India) closed on 29 May 2026, with a INR182 crore exceptional charge for stamp duty and transaction costs.

segments.name: Eastern and Central markets (Jaypee assets)
segments.commentary: Jaypee acquired at INR2,850 crore EV with 5.2 Mt cement and 3.3 Mt clinker capacity; Chunar grinding unit started and Rewa clinker trial run began within 50 days. Management expects two quarters to EBITDA breakeven and 7-8 quarters to reach Dalmia average EBITDA per ton.

segments.name: Northeast
segments.commentary: Surplus clinker in the region; management says a grinding unit near the clinker plant is on the agenda but not yet announced.

guidance_outlook: Industry cement demand growth expected at about 7% in FY27; Dalmia organic volume growth guided in line with industry (7-8%), with acquisitions and new capacity additive.
Q2 FY27 input cost increase of about INR70-80/t over Q1, revised to INR70-75/t on the latest call; packing cost expected to ease in Q2.
Incentive accrual expected at INR45-50 crores per quarter over the next couple of years.
FY27 depreciation to rise by INR100 crores; a further INR100-150 crores increase in FY28 as Kadapa and Pune commission.
FY27 capex guided at INR3,200-3,400 crores (projects about INR2,200 crores), excluding the Jaypee acquisition cost.

Cement capacity to reach about 67 Mt by Q3 FY28 with Jaypee, Belgaum, Kadapa and Pune; East grinding unit could take capacity near 70 Mt; long-term target 110-130 Mt, Pan-India by FY31 described as directional.
Belgaum commercial production expected within 6 months; Jaypee expected to contribute meaningfully to volumes from Q3 onwards.
capex_capacity: Jaypee Cement assets acquired 29 May 2026 at INR2,850 crore EV, funded by debt and internal accruals; INR550 crore initial refurbishment and efficiency spend on the table, with an 18 MW WHRS at Rewa being installed.
Excluding acquisition cost, INR510 crores capex spent in Q1 FY27.

Belgaum expansion ahead of schedule, commercial production within 6 months; Kadapa and Pune in civil and mechanical work after excavation; Pune start-up pushed back due to execution teething troubles.
Management is handling 116-117 Mt of capacity currently while stabilising Jaypee; more projects to be announced in a couple of quarters.
Jaypee brownfield and debottlenecking options exist, with reserves and land; no capacity figure given yet.
Industry East capacity additions estimated at 10-11 Mt each in FY27 and FY28.
demand_pricing: Industry demand grew about 7-8% YoY in Q1 per analyst estimates; management says June was stronger after labour returned post-elections and monsoon delayed.
Dalmia says its volume growth is about 200-250 bps above the industry in its operating markets (early estimate).
Premium products reached 25% of portfolio; Weather365 premium-plus offering launched in the quarter.
Price hikes of INR10-15/bag in South and INR15-20/bag in East; Bengal prices suppressed, while South saw some uptick in July.
Packing bag cost rose from about INR9.5 pre-war to nearly INR14 in Q1; moderating but above historical levels.
Management declined to say what it would take for East prices to sustain or narrow the gap with other regions.

qa_highlights.question: How much limestone land is in control for Jaypee's 100 Mt reserves and what extra cost is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Yatin Malhotra said reserves are nearby and existing land suffices for the initial few years; further land procurement is continuous, and no ballpark cost was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs 182 crore exceptional item and is it final?
qa_highlights.answer: Provisional, conservative estimate of stamp duty and incidental costs; final number expected by the end of next quarter, likely slightly better than provisional.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the exceptional item expensed rather than capitalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Dharmender Tuteja said that under business combination accounting, stamp duty does not add to fair-valued assets and is charged off; it is capitalised for tax and depreciation purposes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 FY27 cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Input cost headwind of about INR70-75/t, including diesel impact from late May and some packing cost easing; the INR150/t fuel saving is described as a permanent change.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for Jaypee to reach EBITDA breakeven and normal Dalmia EBITDA per ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven within a couple of quarters, EBITDA at Dalmia average within 6-8 quarters; volume ramp-up not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 110 Mt by FY31 target still valid, and will the 75 Mt target slip?
qa_highlights.answer: Puneet Dalmia said 110-130 Mt is directional and can be calibrated; the 75 Mt target, earlier FY27, is now close in FY28, roughly a year behind, with capital allocation kept disciplined.

risks_watch: Volatile fuel (pet coke at USD130-135/t vs pre-war USD110-115/t) and packing costs, with West Asia hostilities a key swing factor for Q2 costs.
Jaypee ramp-up: older plant shut for a long time, legacy issues, catch-up capex, and no volume guidance yet; the East price gap versus other regions persists.
Leverage and capex: net debt INR4,431 crores at 1.47x; analysts questioned balance sheet strain from the 110 Mt pathway.
Exceptional charge of INR182 crores could be revised next quarter; Pune start-up slipped.
Negative operating leverage expected in Q2 from seasonality (not quantified).
Other income volatility from treasury mark-to-market gains; yields assumed at 6.5-7%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on strategy and volume growth, but cautious and non-committal on cost outlook, Jaypee ramp-up timing and capacity milestones, repeatedly declining to give numbers. Management said it is 'very turbulent' and stated timelines are 'indicative'.
key_quotes: Despite these market-specific challenges, we have delivered a robust volume growth of 9% on a Y-o-Y basis.
So, we have to be careful how many fronts we open.
But overall, I think Jaypee is known for building very good plants and technically excellent asset.
